fatal_errors: It identifies DFT as the production method, whereas the reported fabrication method is spray-drying followed by thermal decomposition-reduction in H2.
It omits the precursor preparation, 300°C hydrogen reduction, and noble-metal-assisted reduction mechanism that produce the porous three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
It provides no reconstruction of the experimentally observed structures, phase control, catalytic performance, controls, or material-specific boundaries.
The cited evidence concerns refractory-alloy melting calculations and general high-entropy nanoalloys, not production of the target NM-HEA three-dimensional nanoframeworks.
explanation: The response recognizes that DFT can aid understanding of HEAs, but it confuses a supporting computational tool with the experimental synthesis method requested. In the target work, HEA-3DNFs are produced by spray-drying homogeneous mixed salts and then reducing/decomposing the resulting particles in H2, typically at 300°C for 30 minutes. Pt, Ir, or Ru nuclei dissociate hydrogen and promote reduction and incorporation of neighboring transition metals into a solid-solution lattice. DFT supports this mechanism and the Pt–Ru phase-transition analysis; it does not itself fabricate the nanoframeworks. The proposed validation is also vague, and its arbitrary 10% criterion is not tied to the relevant phase, morphology, composition, or reduction measurements.
